input.question: Has the addition of "Drink Responsibly" or "Winners know when to quit" in advertisements actually made any change to alcoholic and gambling addictions?
input.ground_truth: Personally, I don't know any of the statistics. But, I always thought such slogans were more to relive the companies from legal action. Like they could say "Look, we TOLD them to drink responsibly, it isn't our fault he had 20 of our beers and drove".

Okay, let's imagine you have a toy that you really, really like, and sometimes you want to play with it all the time, even when you're supposed to do other things. Now, imagine the toy's box has a sticker that says, "Only play for a little while" or "Take breaks, it's okay!"

These stickers are like the "Drink Responsibly" or "Winners know when to quit" messages on alcohol and gambling ads. The people who make these ads put those messages there to try to help you remember not to play (or drink or gamble) too much.

But, just putting a sticker on the box doesn't always stop you from wanting to play with the toy all the time, especially if you really, really want to. Some people might look at the sticker and remember to take a break, but others might just ignore it and keep playing.

So, those messages help a little bit for some people, but they don't stop everyone from having problems with playing too much, drinking too much, or gambling too much. They're just reminders, but changing big habits is really hard, even with reminders.
